hook.text: A report that takes two hours with a morning deadline somehow takes two weeks when the deadline is next month.

buildup.text: Cyril Northcote Parkinson wrote in 1955: 'Work expands to fill the time available for its completion.'

discovery.text: Without a tight deadline, your brain adds unnecessary steps, rethinks decisions, and perfects things nobody notices.

twist.text: Artificial deadlines work just as well as real ones. Your brain cannot tell the difference if you commit fully.

climax.text: Try cutting your estimated time in half. The constraint forces you to focus on what actually matters.

punchline.text: Shrink the deadline. Watch the waste vanish.

quiz.question: What does Parkinson's Law state?
options: Difficult tasks always take longer than expected
Work expands to fill the time available for it
People work best under extreme pressure
